newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures mixed in extremely thin trade.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures mixed in extremely thin trade.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed early in extremely light pit trade, as the markets awaited for Chicago's National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index, traders and analysts said.

The February Chicago NAPM, which is expected to rise to 56.3, from 55.9, will be a prelude to the overall NAPM index on Monday, and provide further clues on the pace of U.S. economic growth, they said.
They said the tone in most currency futures still remained weak after U.S. Federal Reserve Alan Greenspan said on Wednesday that he couldn't rule out pre-emptive tightening.
However, March yen rose to $0.008350, above the quarter-point retracement level of the 3-1/2-month downmove, after dollar/yen fell through key support at 120.00 spot.
Floor traders had been encouraged in recent days by dollar/yen's ability to hold above the 120.00 level, despite the U.S. dollar's failure to push closer to 125.00.
Overnight dealers attributed the dollar/yen's decline to repatriation ahead of Japan's fiscal year-end on March 31. They also noted good yen buying against other currencies, including the mark.
One currency futures trader said the strong sales of marks against yen indirectly supported the dollar against the mark and Swiss franc.
"The dollar/mark is looking well bid precisely due to the heavy sales of mark/yen overnight," he said.
March marks failed to rise through the pivot point of $0.5926, and is expected to re-test the one-week low of $0.5906 in the near term.
Floor traders said there was little reaction to the revised U.S. fourth-quarter Gross Domestic Product data. The rise in GDP was revised down to 3.9 percent, vs 4.7 percent.
The U.S. Commerce department said the downward revision was due to weaker inventory-building.
Canadian dollar futures were slightly higher, while Australian dollar contracts were lower on continued hedge fund selling from late Thursday.
Mexican peso futures resumed Thursday's sharp slide on mounting concerns about whether or not the U.S. administration would certify Mexico in the war on drugs.

At 0827 CST/1427 GMT, March yen was up $0.000002 at $0.008300, marks were off $0.0012 at $0.5916, Swiss francs were down $0.0026 at $0.6769, sterling were $0.0040 higher at $1.6286, Canadian dollars were $0.0008 higher at $0.7323, Australian dollars were off $0.0008 at $0.7753 and Mexican pesos were down $0.001050 at $0.123200.
